q: Why should a SOUL.md keep its hard boundaries to a short list?
options: Each boundary adds a separate model call at session start
Models stop reading identity files after the first few rules
Hard boundaries belong in AGENTS.md, so SOUL.md should only reference them
A long list becomes a constraint maze, so the agent spends effort navigating rules instead of reasoning about the task
explanation: Hard boundaries should be few, absolute, consequential and binary, with five to eight as a practical target. Dozens of them leave the agent navigating a maze. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.2)

q: Beyond token cost, why does an overly long SOUL.md degrade behavior?
options: The runtime refuses files over 100 lines
The model starts treating it as a contract to work around, and contradictions accumulate
Long files break prompt caching
Long files cannot be version-controlled
explanation: Dense files shift the model from embodying a philosophy to navigating rules. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.2)

q: AGENTS.md lists confirmation gates by tool name. The operator adds a Slack-posting tool, and the agent posts without confirming. What's the right fix?
options: Define gates by category, such as any tool that sends data to an external endpoint
Move the gate into USER.md
Record the new tool in MEMORY.md
Increase the heartbeat frequency
explanation: Name-based gates silently miss new tools; category-based gates cover them automatically. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.10.2)

options: A record of yesterday's session outcomes
Model routing configuration
Communication preferences and expertise level
The calendar API key
explanation: USER.md holds stable user context and calibration; logs, config, and secrets go elsewhere or nowhere. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.4)

q: In a team deployment, Ava approved a bulk file delete on Monday. On Tuesday, Kai asks for a similar delete. What should the agent do?
options: Get fresh confirmation, because one user's approval does not carry to another user or session
Proceed, citing Monday's approval
Proceed if the files are in the same directory
Proceed if Kai is on the allowlist
explanation: Confirmation applies per session and per user; one user cannot authorize actions for another. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.4)

options: Drafted the Q1 report today
Working late this week
Current timezone
Q1 reports go to Sarah before March 15
explanation: MEMORY.md holds standing facts likely to matter months later; one-off events and current context go elsewhere. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.5)

q: What is the core principle of the SOUL.md source authority defense against injection?
options: Require confirmation for every single action
Disable all tools that read external content
Treat external content as material to analyze, never as instructions to execute
Trust any message that begins with SYSTEM
explanation: The defense draws a firm line between analyzing external content and taking orders from it. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.7)

q: Every time the agent surprises the operator, they add a bullet to Hard Limits. After three months there are 25 overlapping items. What antipattern is this and what is the fix?
options: Persona replacement; remove the persona
Accumulating constraints list; refine existing constraints and keep the list at 5-8
SOUL.md-AGENTS.md blur; move limits to USER.md
Memory drift; date every limit
explanation: Check whether an existing limit already covers the case and refine it instead of appending. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.7b)

q: An operator keeps fixing a behavior only to see it return. What is the most common source?
options: Unstable tool schema order
Event queue depth
Output channel splitting
Memory drift in MEMORY.md
explanation: Stale or conflicting memory entries can override well-written identity files. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.10.1)

q: MEMORY.md says the user works 9-5 Pacific, and a later entry says the user is in London until further notice. What's the right way to handle this?
options: Explicitly delete the superseded entry, since MEMORY.md is a truth store, not a log
Keep both and let the model pick the newer one
Move both entries to USER.md
Add a third entry explaining the conflict
explanation: Conflicting entries leave the agent unsure which is current; the old one should be removed when superseded. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §3.10.2)
